chunk_findings.detail: The `[hooks.events]` table only declares `pre_tool` and `post_tool`, but the descriptor’s own `[facts."hooks.events"]` says Vibe has “exactly three events pre_tool, post_tool, post_agent.” If the hook generator emits only the events listed in `[hooks.events]`, a configured Vibe `post_agent` hook will be silently omitted from `.vibe/hooks.toml`; the documented post-agent hook will never run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/harnesses/vibe.toml:23-25

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP example hardcodes `command = "uvx"` with `args = ["ddflow-mcp"]`. On a fresh lane where `ddflow-mcp` is not already installed as a uv tool, following this delta causes Vibe to launch the MCP server through `uvx`, which resolves the package from an index and may install/run an ephemeral environment. That is a network/package-install action triggered by ddflow-generated configuration, contrary to the stated conformance requirement of no installs without operator consent and offline conformance, and it can also fail outright in an offline environment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/vibe.md:25

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that the documented Vibe hook event set is exactly `{"pre_tool": "pre_tool", "post_tool": "post_tool"}`, but the stated documented facts include a `post_agent` hook as well. If the descriptor records that documented `post_agent` event, `H.hooks.events` will contain a third key and this exact-equality assertion fails. If the descriptor omits `post_agent` to make the test pass, the descriptor is wrong because it drops a documented hook event.

chunk_findings.detail: The `verified.unverified` array is supposed to hold only unverified facts, but this entry records a *documented absence*: “session-start and session-end hooks (documented absent)”. A consumer or conformance check that reads `verified.unverified` as the set of unknowns will therefore treat the session-hook gap as unknown rather than as a known absence. That violates the three-valued facts requirement (value, documented absent, unverified): given a check that asks whether session hooks are unverified, the descriptor answers “yes” because of line 129, even though the same file and the research intent say they are documented absent.

chunk_findings.detail: The new generated MCP entry hardcodes `command = "python3"` and `--repo "."`. If `adopt` writes this literally, Vibe launches whatever `python3` is on the server's PATH with the repository path resolved relative to the MCP process's working directory. In a lane where `ddflow` is installed only in a virtualenv or uv-tool environment and not in the system `python3`, `python3 -m ddflow` exits with `No module named ddflow`, so the ddflow MCP server never starts; the operator would have to install into the system interpreter or edit the generated config, contrary to the "already-installed" intent. The relative `--repo .` is also fragile: when Vibe starts the server from the lane home or a subdirectory (the delta itself discusses a lane home pre-trusting a worktree), `.` points at the wrong directory instead of the adopted worktree. The generated entry should use the resolved interpreter/entry point and an absolute or templated repo path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/drivers/deltas/vibe.md:25
